answer: Coordination-Density Pricing. Each agent identity must anchor its actions to a publicly auditable coordination record: every pairwise interaction is logged, and an identity's price scales with how much unique coordination it shares with others. Fresh identities that only interact with each other form a dense cluster, so their per-action price rises sharply—each sybil pays more than the timber of a real transaction. To keep costs low, identities must diversify across a comet of independent counterparties, which sybils cannot cheaply fake.
